questions.solutionHtml:
font-size:12pt">Option A. True - Abrasions occur when the skin rubs or scrapes against a rough surface, leading to the removal of the superficial skin layers.

questions.stemHtml: A patient has presented to your outpatient department with complaints of cough and fever for the past five days. During her examination, you observe a contusion behind her right ear. What type of contusion is depicted in the picture?
questions.solutionHtml:
ir="ltr" lang="EN" style="font-size:12.0pt">Ans. D) Ectopic bruise

 

Explanation:

 

Ectopic bruising, also known as percolated or migratory contusion - Refers to a particular type of contusion where bruises do not necessarily appear directly at the site of impact. Instead, blood will track along the fascial planes (or between muscle layers) which form the least resistance and may appear where the tissue layers become superficial (ectopic bruising or percolated or migratory contusion).

 

Haemorrhages in the soft tissues around the eyes and in the eyelids (spectacle haematoma; black eye), may be caused by (l) direct trauma, such as a punch in the eye, (2) blunt impact to the forehead, the blood gravitating downwards over the supraorbital bridge, (3) fracture of the floor of the anterior fossa of the skull.

 

A bruise behind the ear may indicate a basal fracture, rather than a direct blow behind the ear. Other example is "Battle's sign" seen in jaw fractures, where a bruise may appear in the neck.

 

Educational Objective:

 

An ectopic bruise is a specific type of contusion that does not appear at the actual site of impact but instead appears in a different location. This happens because the blood from the injury site migrates along the fascial planes to an area where the tissue layers are more superficial.

questions.stem: A forensic examiner is evaluating a body found in a remote area. Among the various injuries noted, there are multiple contusions on different parts of the body. In determining the nature of these injuries, the examiner must distinguish between true facts and misconceptions about contusions. Which of the following statements about contusions is NOT true?

options.label: A
options.text: It is due to the rupture of blood vessels with the overlying skin remaining intact.

options.label: B
options.text: The involved area is elevated above the surrounding skin level.

options.label: D
options.text: The age of the injury can be determined based on its appearance.

questions.solutionHtml:
"text-align:justify"> 

Explanation:

 

Option A. Due to the rupture of blood vessels with intact skin - True. Contusions occur when blood vessels are damaged under the skin, but the skin surface remains intact.

 

Option B. The involved area is elevated - True. In contusion, there is a painful swelling, and crushing or tearing of the subcutaneous tissues usually without destruction of the skin. The extravasated blood is diffusely distributed through the tissue spaces, and the margins are blurred.

 

Option D. Age of injury can be determined - True. The color changes in a contusion over time, progressing from red/blue to green to yellow/brown, can help estimate the age of the injury.

 

 

Educational Objective:

 

Contusions, or bruises, are caused by the rupture of blood vessels beneath the intact skin, leading to the accumulation of blood in the surrounding tissues. One key characteristic of contusions is that they typically do not have clearly defined margins. The spread of blood into the surrounding tissues causes the margins to be blurry or irregular. This contrasts with other types of injuries, such as lacerations or incised wounds, which usually have more clearly defined margins.

 

Ref: Reddy 33/e. Pg 184

questions.solutionHtml:

Lacerations are three-dimensional injuries, characterized by their depth in addition to length and breadth, is crucial for forensic evaluations and determining the mechanism of injury.

Among the various injuries sustained, one is particularly notable for its unique presentation: the skin and soft tissue appear to be forcibly torn away in a manner resembling flaying. Which type of laceration in the following options is most commonly associated with this appearance of flaying?
questions.solutionHtml:
-family:"Calibri",sans-serif">Explanation:

 

Option A. Split - Occur when soft tissues are sandwiched between a hard unyielding deeper structure and the agent applying the force. Scalp lacerations occur due to the tissues being crushed between the skull and some hard object.

 

Option B. Stretched - Result from a heavy forceful frictional impact of blunt forces exercising localized ‘pressure with pull’. Overstretching of the skin and subcutaneous tissues may cause lacerations with flapping of the skin, which may indicate the direction of application of force. They are seen in run over by motor vehicle, kicking and in compound fractures.

 

Option D. Tear - Tearing of skin and subcutaneous tissue can occur from localized impact by or against some hard, irregular object like car door handle, radiator mascot or from blows with broken glass bottles.

 

Educational Objective:

 

Avulsion injury occurs when the wheel moves over a fleshy part causing degloving of skin and subcutaneous tissue, by tearing it away from underlying tissues. It is also called ‘flaying injury’, and is seen mostly in legs, arms and scalp.

questions.solutionHtml:
-size:11pt">Option B. Tear - Tear lacerations are caused by an object catching and pulling the skin, resulting in ragged edges, which are unlike the clean cuts of an incised wound.

 

Option C. Avulsed - Avulsed lacerations involve the forcible tearing away of tissue and often present with irregular, jagged edges, not typically resembling the smooth edges of incised wounds.

 

Option D. Stretched - Stretched lacerations occur when the skin is overstretched and tears, usually producing irregular or jagged edges, which do not mimic the smooth, clean-cut appearance of an incised wound.

 

Educational Objective

 

Split lacerations can closely mimic incised wounds despite being caused by blunt force, is essential for accurately determining the mechanism of injury. They can be differentiated from incised wounds by following:

 

  • Due to blunt force, there is usually associated abrasions and contusions in the margins
  • Depth of the wound presents bridges of irregularly torn tissue, blood vessels and nerves, etc.

pt">Explanation:

an dir="ltr" lang="EN" style="font-size:12.0pt">Option A. Contusions: These are bruises or injuries typically caused by blunt force trauma, not by sharp cutting weapons.

The heavy nature of the weapon contributes to the severity and depth of the wound.

 

Wounds caused by sharp edged and pointed weapons are of four types: Incised wound, Chop wound, Stab wound and Therapeutic/diagnostic wound

tyle="text-align:justify">Option B. Stomach: While blunt trauma in explosions can affect abdominal organs, it is less likely than injuries to more vulnerable structures like the eardrum or lungs.

questions.stem: Following an explosion on a naval vessel, several crew members sustain injuries. questions.solutionHtml:
-align:justify">

Option C. Liver: The liver, being a solid organ, is less susceptible to the immediate pressure wave effects of an underwater blast compared to gas-filled organs like the GIT or lungs. Injuries to the liver are more likely due to secondary mechanisms, such as blunt trauma.

To understand that the gastrointestinal tract is the most common site of injury in underwater blast.

questions.stemHtml: During an autopsy of a 45-year-old male who suffered a fatal fall from a significant height, the medical officer observes a distinctive pattern of skull fracture. The base of the skull has a linear fracture extending bilaterally from the foramen magnum along the petrous ridges of the temporal bones, resembling a bilateral longitudinal separation. Given the nature of the injury and the observed fracture pattern, what is the classification of this skull fracture?

options.label: A
options.text: Ring fracture of base of skull

options.label: B
options.text: Hinge fracture of base of skull

questions.answerText: Hinge fracture of base of skull
questions.solutionHtml:
strong>transverse fracture of the base of the skull that completely splits it and divide it into two halves, each moving independently of each other like a hinge (‘nodding face’ sign).

 

Explanation:

 

Option A. Ring fracture of base of skull often seen in the skull, where the bone breaks in a circular pattern around foramen magnum. The picture above have a transverse fracture that completely splits it making it a hinge fracture, hence this option is incorrect.

 

Option C. Comminuted fracture of skull: is when two or more intersecting lines of fracture divide the bone into three or more fragments resembling a spider web or mosaic pattern this is not the case in this picture hence this option is incorrect.

 

Option D. Depressed fracture of skull: When a portion of fractured bone is driven inwards to a distance equivalent to the thickness of the skull table, it is known as depressed fracture. The picture in the question have a transverse fracture dividing the base of the skull and is not a depressed fracture hence this option is incorrect.

 

Educational Objective:

 

‘Hinge’ # (also called Motorcyclist #): Linear fracture passes across the middle cranial fossa, separating the skull base into Ant and post halves. Occurs Severe Force to side of head (e.g. in motorcycle accidents). Such fractures are commonly associated with injuries of the brain stem, especially pontomedullary tears.

questions.stem: A forensic expert is presented with the skull of an infant who suffered a head trauma. Upon examination, the expert notes a fracture which is known as Diastatic fracture. The Diastatic fracture refers to fracture through?

Explanation:

 

Diastatic #: Separation of cranial sutures

 

  • Seen in young children (due to non-union of sutures)
  • Causes: 1) Trauma   2) Pathology (e.g. Intracranial tumor)
  • Most commonly sagittal sutures get separated

 

 

 

Educational Objective:

 

Diastatic or Sutural Fractures: Separation of the sutures occur only in young persons, due to a blow on head with blunt weapon. It may occur alone but often is associated with fracture. It is usually seen in the sagittal suture. They are particularly common in traffic accidents. They also occur secondary to increased intracranial pressure with resulting splitting of sutures.

="font-size:12.0pt">Ans. A) Murder

  2. Passive Defence Wounds: When Victim just takes the weapon on his parts in order to protect himself from the attack.

Defense wounds, characterized by injuries on the hands and forearms that result from defensive actions, are often observed in cases of homicide. questions.stem: During an autopsy at a medical college hospital, you, a forensic expert, are examining the body of a 40-year-old man who was found in an alleyway. Among various injuries, you notice a specific wound on the victim's arm. This wound is irregular, with uneven margins and varying depths. Notably, you observe strands of connective tissue, blood vessels, and nerves that appear to bridge across the base and sides of the wound. These findings are critical to your assessment and report. What type of wound typically presents with such tissue bridges?
questions.solutionHtml:
e="font-family:"Calibri",sans-serif">Ans. C) Laceration

 

Explanation:

 

Features of lacerated wound:

 

  1. Swallow Tails: The margins of lacerated wound may show tearing of the extremities at angles diverging from the main laceration, the so-called ‘swallow tails.
  2. Abrasion or bruising in the margins due to blunt force
  3. Tissue Bridges: Depth of the wound presents bridges of irregularly torn fibrous tissue, blood vessels and nerves, etc.
  4. Soiling of the wound by mud, sand, vegetation, hair, fibers, etc.
  5. Less Bleeding as compared to incised wound: Lacerated wounds do not  bleed  much  as  the  vessels  are  crushed and torn but not cut evenly, thus facilitating hemostasis  to  some  extent.
  6. Crushed hair bulb: Lacerations over the hairy areas will show hair bulbs crushed

 

The above features helps to differentiate lacerated wound from Incised wound, especially in cases of “Incised looking lacerated wound”

 

The below image shows an “Incised looking lacerated wound”. Tissue bridges confirm that it is a lacerated wound.

 

 

Educational Objective:

 

Laceration can be differentiated from incised wounds by following:

 

  1. Due to blunt force, there is usually associated abrasions and contusions in the margins
  2. Depth of the wound presents bridges of irregularly torn tissue, blood vessels and nerves, etc.

 

Note - An opposite variety is Lacerated looking incised wound:  It is an incised wound, which looks like lacerated wound. It occurs in areas where skin folds are loose, like in axilla, scrotum etc. Here even an injury produced by sharp weapon appears as if it has irregular margins.

questions.stem: Counter coup injury is seen in:

Ans. A. Brain

 

Counter coup injury refers to a traumatic injury that occurs on the side of the brain opposite to the site of impact. It is caused by the brain rebounding against the inner surface of the skull after an initial impact. Counter coup injuries typically occur as a result of high-velocity forces that cause the brain to move rapidly within the skull, leading to additional injury on the opposite side of the brain from the initial impact. These injuries can include contusions, hemorrhages, lacerations, or other forms of damage. Counter coup injuries are commonly observed in situations such as motor vehicle accidents or falls where the head undergoes sudden deceleration or acceleration forces.

questions.stem: Compound used as primer in weapon is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Potassium chlorate

 

The compound used as a primer in a weapon is potassium chlorate (option a). A primer is a component of ammunition that is responsible for initiating the firing sequence. It is typically located in the base of the cartridge case and is ignited by a firing pin or striking mechanism.

 

Potassium chlorate is a chemical compound that contains oxygen and is highly reactive. It is commonly used as an oxidizer in the primer composition of ammunition. When the primer is struck, it generates a small flame or spark due to the rapid decomposition of potassium chlorate. This flame then ignites the propellant, initiating the combustion process that propels the projectile out of the firearm.

 

The other options mentioned - sulfur (option b), potassium nitrate (option c), and nitrocellulose (option d) - are also commonly used in the manufacturing of ammunition and propellants, but they are not specifically used as primers. Therefore, the correct answer is option a, potassium chlorate.
